nodes.referent: The physical theory of relativity in physics -- special relativity (1905: constancy of the speed of light and the unification of space and time into spacetime, replacing Newtonian absolute space and time) and general relativity (1915: gravity as the curvature of spacetime) -- not the general philosophical doctrine of relativism, not a single specific equation or paper, and not the Lorentz-transformation mathematics considered on its own apart from the physical reinterpretation Einstein gave it.
nodes.source_hint: Wikipedia 'Theory of relativity' / 'Special relativity' / 'General relativity'; Encyclopedia Britannica 'relativity'.
nodes.note: Re-admission of a node declined in concept-wave3-v1 (recorded in foundry/rejections.json) solely for lack of an Einstein person node ('re-admissible once person:albert-einstein exists'); that gap is now closed. Henri Poincare (already a reviewed node) and Albert Einstein both receive edges to this concept in the companion edges.proposed.json for this batch, positioned per clause-6 v2 rather than as competing founder claims -- see that file for the reasoning.
nodes.rationale: Re-admits the concept-wave3-v1 rejection now that person:albert-einstein exists in the corpus: the node was withheld only because its sole available person link was Poincare, and the rejection record itself named this as a node-task gap, not an edge-task or concept-worthiness problem. The theory of relativity is a foundational, canonical concept of modern physics with a clean structural home under field:physics.
nodes.uncertainty: I have not live-verified this node's disambiguation from adjacent physics/philosophy homonyms (special relativity and general relativity as possible separate structured items, philosophical relativism, or narrower Lorentz-transformation-only items) this session. The sibling concepts admitted in concept-wave3-v1 (entropy in particular) needed a targeted, non-obvious disambiguation search before their identity resolved cleanly, so this is a real risk class for this node, not a formality.
